description: The growth rate of Collatz trajectories is governed by the ratio of 3-multiplications to 2-divisions, characterized by ln(3)/ln(2) ≈ 1.585. Angeltveit uses the rational approximation 485/306 > ln(3)/ln(2) to derive a tight arithmetic criterion: if 485*f <= 306*k (where f = odd steps, k = total steps), then T^k(n) < n for n > 99781. This converts a floating-point comparison into exact integer arithmetic, critical for GPU verification correctness.
analogical_connections: Continued fraction approximation in Diophantine analysis — rational bounds for irrational quantities
Fixed-point arithmetic in DSP — replace floating-point with exact integer ratios for determinism
Lyapunov exponent estimation — rational bounds on growth rates in dynamical systems
implementation_hypothesis: Replace all floating-point comparisons in the sieve with the integer test: 485*f_count <= 306*step_count. Precompute the dip values dip_B(m) = max_{k=0..B}(306*k - 485*f_k(m)) for bitvector construction. For GPU Step 3, maintain running counts of odd/even steps and check the integer inequality after each block of 16 steps.
experiment_seed: Compare the tightness of 485/306 against other convergents of ln(3)/ln(2) (e.g., 306191/193205). Measure: false-positive rate (numbers that pass the bound but actually descend), computational cost of the tighter bound. Test whether using the next convergent measurably improves pruning rate.
